newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Gov to propose cutting property taxes - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Gov to propose cutting property taxes - paper.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki plans to propose a sweeping, multi-year reduction in property taxes in his State of the State Address to the legislature Wednesday, according to New York Post.
The paper, citing sources, said the governor's new proposal is expected to save localities and cost the state "at least" hundreds of millions of dollars over the next four years.
The plan is expected to help refute attacks expected from Democrats on Pataki's three-year, $3.6 billion personal income tax reduction plan, which is in its final year the paper said.

Sharply rising property taxes are a major concern to homeowners outside New York City, and Pataki plans to offer the city a separate source of new state revenue in lieu of property tax relief, the Post said.
Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Renssalaer, has proposed a statewide reduction in property taxes that would provide extra lottery revenues to localities that freeze their property taxes.

In his address on Wednesday, Pataki also is expected to reiterate his call to abolish parole for violent criminals, urge targeted tax cuts, including a reduction in the state tax on electric utilities, and argue that his first two years in office have "produced a monumental turnaround" in the attitude of the state's private employers, which will help create more jobs and boost tax collections.
